name: Chicken stir fry with glass noodles & vegetables

source.author: User's recipe
source.notes: Analyzed from a pasted ingredient list. Assumptions flagged: glass (mung bean) noodles '1 cup' taken as ~100 g dry; NO cooking oil was listed so ~1 tbsp assumed for a stir fry; sprouts amount ~100 g; champignon 'basket' ~250 g; sauces measured as tbsp. Servings assumed 5 for the batch.

serving_desc: ≈380 g (big batch ÷5). Whole batch: 1 kg chicken + all veg + noodles
steps: Stir-fry the chicken breast (cut to strips) until cooked through.
Add onion, garlic, cabbage, mushrooms; stir-fry until softened.
Add the soaked glass noodles, sweet soy, pad thai sauce and soy sauce; toss to coat.
Add the bean sprouts and cook them through (do not leave raw); finish with green onions.

him.verdict: An outstanding cutting/muscle meal on the numbers — extremely lean and protein-dense (~49 g protein for ~408 kcal, ~12.9 g protein per 100 g), loaded with low-calorie high-volume veg, and carrying selenium + zinc (sperm micros). The only real knock is SODIUM: three salty sauces (soy + sweet soy + pad thai) stack to ~620 mg/serving, and the sweet soy/pad thai add some sugar. Refined glass noodles are a minor carb, small vs the protein/veg.
suggested_mods: Cut sodium: use low-sodium soy or drop the plain soy to 1 tbsp — you'll barely notice with sweet soy + pad thai already in
Measure any cooking oil (~1 tbsp) — it's the main hidden-calorie swing since none was listed
Already great; add more cabbage/sprouts for even more volume on a hungry day

her_preconception.verdict: Good preconception profile — lean protein + choline (~128 mg), folate from the cabbage/sprouts/onion, selenium, and iron paired with the veg's vitamin C. Two advisories, both easy: cook the sprouts fully (raw sprouts are a pregnancy caution), and the sodium is on the high side.
prenatal_highlights: selenium; iron paired with vegetable vitamin C

safety_advisories.note: Bean sprouts: raw/undercooked sprouts carry a bacterial risk (listeria/salmonella/E. coli) that matters in pregnancy. In this dish they should be cooked through, not tossed in raw at the very end.
safety_advisories.swap: cook sprouts fully, or omit once actively trying/pregnant

safety_advisories.note: High sodium (~620 mg/serving from three sauces) — worth easing during pregnancy.

suggested_mods: Make sure the sprouts are cooked through
Use low-sodium soy to bring the salt down
Keep the cabbage/onion/sprouts — they're the folate here
